This notice describes the website preview you are viewing and the project-brief tool it contains.

Updated 22 October 2026

What you can enter

The brief tool asks for your name, company or property, email address, project location, area of interest and a project description. Use only information you are comfortable including in a project brief.

Where your brief goes

The tool prepares text within the current browser tab. It does not send the brief to GEM or to an enquiry service. The site does not save the form to browser storage. Reloading or clearing the page removes its working form state; your browser may separately offer autofill.

Copying and downloading

Copying places the prepared brief on your device’s clipboard. Downloading saves a text file to your device. You control any later sharing of that text or file. Clearing the form does not remove a downloaded file or clear your clipboard.

Cookies and analytics

This preview does not set analytics or marketing cookies, use tracking scripts, or request third-party fonts. The logo and fonts are served with the site. Your browser makes the requests needed to load the pages and assets; the serving environment may record technical request information.

Information to leave out

Do not enter payment details, identity-document numbers, health information, confidential guest information or other sensitive personal data. This tool is intended for an initial business brief.

Operator and privacy contact — pending

Operator: [PUBLIC OPERATOR NAME — PENDING]. Privacy contact: [PRIVACY CONTACT EMAIL — PENDING]. These are placeholders, not confirmed contact details.

Hosting logs — pending

Logging services: [PENDING]. Access to records: [PENDING]. Retention period: [PENDING]. The actual hosting-log practices have not yet been confirmed.

Before public launch

A public service needs a confirmed business contact, hosting arrangements, retention practices and any receiving enquiry service reflected in its privacy notice. This preview notice covers the current local tool; it is not a statement about a future service.
